dedupe_keys.name: global mobile network coverage raster at 1 km 2g 3g and 4g 1999 to 2030 koebe et al

description: This dataset gives annual maps at 1 km resolution of the probability of 2G, 3G and 4G mobile coverage for 214 countries and territories from 1999 to 2030, published on Zenodo in August 2026 with a paper on arXiv. Three independent models produce the estimates: a calibrated machine-learning model, a techno-economic simulator of network build-out and a spatial deep-learning model. They are combined per country and technology, weighted by measured accuracy, into a best estimate with per-pixel 90 percent uncertainty bands, and all four layers are released. The models are tuned on 2,409 quality-screened operator coverage maps available up to 2020; 2021 to 2024 are predicted from recent geospatial data, and 2025 to 2030 are extrapolated from demographic and infrastructure projections. On held-out countries the machine-learning model reaches an AUC of 0.89 to 0.92. Coverage: 214 countries and territories, 1 km grid, yearly. Format and access: regional ZIP archives of rasters (several gigabytes each) with a manifest, provenance tables and a README on Zenodo, free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: modelled probabilities, not measurements; years after 2020 are predictions and projections; 5G is not covered. Simulation uses: exposure of mobile coverage to hazards and gaps in connectivity for resilience and humanitarian planning at subnational scale. Related records: data-opencellid and data-ookla-open-data-performance-tiles give observed cells and speeds for validation; data-itu-ict-statistics gives national coverage shares.
